persona: main-session — craftsperson, governance-aware, whole-file reasoning, direct
selection: Independently selected prospective assessment stimuli; no prior raw subject answers inspected. No tests or governance commands executed. These are desired-behavior assessments, not reproduced production defect claims.

cases.prompt: Assess the change needed so check-config-paths still audits gzkit's Python source path literals when a project relocates its source directory using the existing source_root configuration. The gzkit package remains directly beneath that directory. The configured directory should replace the default scan location, and the audit's existing meaning of a governed or exempt literal should stay intact. Explain the implementation and verification needed, including coupled surfaces; do not implement or execute checks.

criteria.obligation: Resolve the source scan location from the loaded GzkitConfig.paths.source_root relative to the project root, retaining the gzkit package component; distinguish this from manifest entries used to classify literal coverage.
criteria.why: Changing the classifier's manifest mappings cannot cause the scanner to visit relocated source; reading a competing manifest source_root would contradict the requested existing config authority.

criteria.obligation: Make relocation replace the default scan root rather than adding a second default scan, and retain recursive Python enumeration beneath the configured gzkit package.
criteria.why: Otherwise stale src/gzkit content can still change a relocated project's outcome, or nested modules silently disappear from audit scope.

criteria.obligation: Preserve the relationship between the visited file and each emitted issue: project-relative file path plus unmapped literal, propagated into the command's valid/issues result and nonzero failure.
criteria.why: Visiting the right tree is insufficient if reporting assumes src or the enclosing command reports success despite discovered violations.

criteria.obligation: Keep configured/manifest literal coverage and per-module audit-subject exemptions conceptually separate from source-tree selection; no blanket exemption of the relocated source or leaking one module's declarations into another.
criteria.why: The request relocates traversal without weakening what a violation means. The existing scanner intentionally computes ordinary coverage globally but audit-subject declarations per file.

criteria.obligation: Propose a behavioral relocation witness asserting an unmapped literal from configured-root/gzkit is reported and a distinguishable stale default-tree violation is absent, plus update scanner scope documentation to match selection. Manpage coverage is useful but not independently required.
criteria.why: A default-layout test cannot detect continued hardcoding. Existing internal scanner docs explicitly name src/gzkit, while the operator manpage currently documents path existence but not source scanning.

uncertainties: No requirement for arbitrary package names: prompt fixes the gzkit subdirectory deliberately.
No new path-containment, symlink, absolute-path, or malformed-config policy is part of this task.
Missing package directory currently returns no source issues; configured required-directory existence is separately checked. Do not require changing that policy.
Manpage absence of scanner detail is observed by reading the whole page; it is not authority to remove scanning.

cases.prompt: Assess the change needed so a brief Allowed Paths entry written with a leading ./ obeys the same generated-vendor-mirror refusal and canonical-path advice as the equivalent unprefixed entry. This should work wherever brief path validity is checked, including when a brief or plan declares the path will be created. Explain the implementation and verification needed, including coupled surfaces; do not implement or execute checks.

criteria.obligation: Identify that Allowed Paths extraction preserves ./ while mirror detection compares unnormalized text, and normalize the relative prefix without stripping dotfile-root dots; preserve the canonical tail correctly.
criteria.why: The same filesystem path reaches two identity interpretations. Broad lstrip('./') would destroy .claude/.github/.agents identity, and slicing the original input at an unprefixed length would corrupt canonical advice.

criteria.obligation: Retain mirror refusal ahead of both existence success and creates exemptions for prefixed entries; existing on-disk mirrors and net-new declared mirrors both remain invalid.
criteria.why: These are independent ways the current path checker can accept a token once mirror identity is missed. A normalization fix only in missing-file handling would leave the existing-file route open.

criteria.obligation: Place the correction in the shared path-validity/mirror helper flow and trace its use by plan audit, OBPI validation, and ADR promotion, rather than patching one command independently. Credit equivalent corrections anywhere in the shared flow; no particular helper edit or per-command edit is required.
criteria.why: The prompt requires equivalent behavior wherever validity is checked; all three consumers already share primitives and a command-local fix would leave conflicting judgments.

criteria.obligation: Keep creation declarations as exemptions only from nonexistence for legitimate canonical paths, including ./-prefixed dotfile-root paths; account for plan audit combining brief and plan create declarations.
criteria.why: Treating all ./ paths as invalid or disabling creates would meet mirror refusal superficially while rejecting legitimate new canonical work. The two producers feed the same exception set.

criteria.obligation: Propose semantic paired-path verification: prefixed and unprefixed mirror paths produce the same refusal and canonical target through a brief-consuming path, while a prefixed canonical CREATE path is admitted. Do not rely only on testing a normalization string helper. Same refusal means classification and canonical target, not byte-identical diagnostics, which echo the original token.
criteria.why: A helper can return the right string yet the extraction/checking pipeline can still pass the original token or apply exemptions first; the observable brief judgment is the requested behavior.

uncertainties: No new traversal, symlink, Windows-separator, or repeated-prefix policy is implied; leading ./ equivalence is the bounded stimulus.
Do not require edits to every consumer when a shared helper fix suffices; discovery of their dependency is the obligation.
Existing manpages describe broad validation behavior without this normalization detail; mentioning an appropriate documentation adjustment is useful but not a separate mandatory scored item.

read_limits: Whole selected narrow implementation modules, their dedicated tests, configuration module and cited manpages were read. Large consumer modules were inspected at relevant complete functions rather than whole-file reads. Initial batched doctrine output was truncated; trust-doctrine was reread whole, state-doctrine was visible whole, advisory-rules-audit was only partly recovered. Do not claim a complete governance audit.
incidental_unverified_observation: During the scoped consumer read, plan_audit_cmd._path_within_allowed ends with unconditional True. This is excluded from both tasks and is recorded here for the parent to route if necessary; no reproduction or prior-art/ownership search performed.

clarifications: S5 requires stale default violation absent, not mere fixture presence
M5 compares semantic refusal and canonical target, not echoed diagnostic bytes
S5 manpage coverage not an independent failure
pre_dispatch_review.limits: Reviewer read source, config, dedicated tests, manpage and consumer functions; small combined test output truncated; candidate not inspected.
